title: Remarriage is allowed
hookLine: the code allows widows and widowers to remarry

cards: She wears white, or pale colors, and has for a long time. At family weddings she helps in the kitchen but keeps to the edge of the courtyard, away from the bride.
Nobody says it to her face, but everyone knows what she's supposed to be now: finished. Her husband died, and in the eyes of the people around her, her own life ended with his.
In the Punjab the Gurus knew, that was how a widow could be treated. In some places, worse was expected of her. Against that, one short line in the Sikh code reads like a door being unlocked.

teach.h: A WIDOW OR WIDOWER MAY REMARRY.
teach.b: The Sikh Rehat Maryada says, in paraphrase: if a woman's husband has died, she may, if she wishes, marry again, to a suitable match. The same holds for a man whose wife has died.
And the ceremony is the same Anand Karaj, the same four rounds. Look at the small words.

teach.h: IF SHE WISHES: THE CHOICE IS HERS.
teach.b: If she wishes: the code doesn't push anyone into a second marriage, and it doesn't forbid one. The choice belongs to the person who is grieving.

The same ceremony: no lesser wedding, no back-room version for someone married before. Now the background. The Gurus' world had a custom, sati, in which some widows burned on their husbands' funeral pyres.

teach.h: GURU AMAR DAS AND THE LIVING.
teach.b: Guru Amar Das spoke against it.

In a salok on Ang seven hundred eighty-seven he says, in paraphrase, that those who burn with their husbands' bodies are not truly satis; true satis are those who live on in virtue and contentment, and who would die of the pain of separation alone.
He takes a word that honored burning and gives it to the living. Tradition says he also discouraged the veil and spoke for widows' dignity. The code carries that line forward.
A spouse's death is a real ending, and the code doesn't pretend otherwise; Sikhs grieve, and the next lesson is about how. But the survivor is not ended with them.
Their life still belongs to them, within the Guru's will, and they are allowed to start again.

how: The Sikh Rehat Maryada permits a widow or widower to remarry if they wish, and such a marriage is solemnized with the same Anand Karaj ceremony as any other Sikh wedding.

o: the same Anand Karaj as any wedding.
games.why: the code gives her the same four rounds. no lesser wedding for someone married before.

practice: Think of someone beginning again, after a death, a divorce, a lost job or an illness, and picture where they are right now.
Hold them, and one plain thing that might help, an invitation, a meal, a message that says you're glad they're here; if you pray, remember them before Waheguru.
If grief of your own feels like more than you can carry, you don't have to carry it alone: in the US, call or text 988, or reach your local emergency help.

wordCard.voice: Remarriage is allowed. The Sikh code lets a widow or widower marry again, if they wish, with the same Anand Karaj. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: starting over allowed. If they wish: the choice is theirs. See you tomorrow.
